correctness.rationale: Choose bases and a base \(B\) larger than every factor dimension, then assign basis weight \(jB^{i-1}\) in factor \(i\). Base-\(B\) uniqueness makes all tensor-coordinate weights distinct, so the ambient projective fixed locus is exactly the coordinate tensor lines. All such lines are decomposable and hence lie in every \(\sigma_r(X)\), while no other fixed point can occur. The singular Euler-localization lemma is proved using Rosenlicht stratification: every nonfixed piece is a locally trivial \(\mathbb C^*\)-bundle and therefore has compactly supported Euler characteristic zero. Thus every projective secant has Euler characteristic \(\prod_i a_i\), and additivity gives zero compactly supported Euler characteristic for every exact border-rank stratum above rank one. No dimension, nondefectivity, smoothness, or stabilization assumption is used.

value.rationale: Higher Segre secant varieties are the fundamental projective border-rank loci for general tensors and are central in algebraic complexity and tensor decomposition. Their dimensions, equations, and singularities vary strongly with the rank parameter, so complete constancy of ordinary Euler characteristic is a non-obvious structural limitation of this basic topological invariant. The exact-stratum consequence is stronger: every border-rank layer above rank one has compactly supported Euler characteristic zero, uniformly in every tensor format with at least three factors. This identifies a natural invariant that provably cannot detect higher border rank and supplies an exact topological constraint on all such strata.
